title: Many true believers lack full certainty before death because they look too much at their unworthiness
source_text: XVIII. Itaque non pauci sunt syncera fide in Christum praediti, & per consequens vere Deo reconciliati, qui tamen de accepta gratia certi non sunt, & quidam ante mortis articulum certitudinem illam non assequuntur. Quod non fit quia circa veritatem promissionum divinarum haesitent, sed quia nimium spectant propriam indignitatem atque infirmitatem.
pass_a_gloss: And so not a few are endowed with sincere faith in Christ, and consequently are truly reconciled to God, who yet are not certain of received grace, and some do not attain that certainty before the point of death. Which happens not because they hesitate about the truth of the divine promises, but because they look too much at their own unworthiness and infirmity.
pass_b_english: Sincere believers may lack full certainty even until death.
The cause is fixation on personal unworthiness, not distrust of God’s promises.
